title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Assignment data (work file, student id, course, submission timestamp) transmitted from Student to Grades Portal Web App could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive academic information.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard HTTPS is not guaranteed; if TLS is used, this threat is mitigated.

title: Linkability of Submission Data
description: Data in transit could be linked across multiple submissions or combined with other data sources to identify the student and correlate their academic activities.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether metadata is stripped during transmission.

title: Excessive Data Collection at Destination
description: Grades Portal Web App may collect and store more data than necessary for the assignment submission purpose, including work files and timestamps that could be retained longer than needed.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard academic portal practices; actual data retention policies unknown.

title: Student Identification from Stored Data
description: The system stores student id, course, and submission data which could be used to identify the student and link their academic records across different contexts.
uncertainty_note: Standard practice for academic systems; identification is inherent to the purpose.

title: Credential Compromise During Login
description: Student's login credentials used to access the submission process could be compromised, allowing unauthorized access to submit assignments on behalf of the student.
uncertainty_note: Depends on authentication mechanism strength (e.g., password vs. SSO vs. MFA).

title: Identifier exposure in transit
description: The data flow contains student id, course, file reference, and requesting role - all unique identifiers that can identify the student. These identifiers are transmitted in transit between P1 and P2, creating a risk that they could be intercepted or logged by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or access controls
uncertainty_note: Using I.2.1.1 from context [1] as it directly matches the identifier nature of the data

title: Processing of identified data at destination
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes identified data (student id, course, file reference). This processing could expose student identity to unauthorized personnel or systems within P2, or create additional derived identifiers through processing.
assumptions: P2 processes the data without sufficient access controls or data minimization
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 from context [3] as it matches the processing of identified data scenario

title: Linkability of student to submissions and grades
description: The combination of student id, course, and file reference in the data flow enables linking the student to their specific submissions and grades. This creates a persistent link that could be exploited to track student activities across systems or time.
assumptions: The identifiers are stable and can be correlated across different contexts
uncertainty_note: Standard LINDDUN linkability node L.1.1 applied based on the nature of the identifiers in the flow

title: Unnecessary Data Storage in Assignment Store
description: The Assignment Store (DS1) stores personal data (student id, course, submission time) that may be retained longer than necessary for the grading process, creating potential for future unauthorized access or disclosure beyond the immediate grading purpose.
assumptions: Data retention policies may not be strictly enforced; the stored data could be accessed by personnel or systems beyond the immediate grading workflow.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard data retention practices may not be in place

title: Linkability via Submission Metadata
description: The data flow contains metadata (student id, course, submission time) that could be used to link the student to their course enrollment and submission patterns, potentially enabling profiling or correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Metadata about the student's course and submission timing could be correlated with other systems or data sources.
uncertainty_note: Assuming metadata is not adequately anonymized or protected during transit

title: Student Identification in Transit
description: Student identification data is transmitted in the data flow, creating a risk that the student could be identified during data transfer if the flow is intercepted or logged.
assumptions: Data in transit may not be adequately encrypted or protected against interception.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard encryption may not be applied to all data flows

title: Identification of teacher during login
description: Teacher's identity is processed when logging in to access the submission queue, creating an identifiable data point that links the teacher to their review activities.

title: Linkability of teacher identity with submission data
description: Metadata about which teacher is reviewing which submissions could be used to link the teacher's identity with specific student submissions, potentially revealing patterns or associations.

title: Potential disclosure of submission data
description: The system stores and processes submission data received from the teacher, which could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data retention policies.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student data to teacher
description: The Grades Portal Web App shares student names, work content, and submission times with the teacher. If the teacher is not properly authorized or if access controls are weak, student data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.

title: Data integrity compromised in transit
description: Student work content and submission data could be altered or tampered with during transmission from the portal to the teacher, potentially affecting the authenticity of the grades and submissions.

title: Teacher mishandling of student data
description: The teacher, as the destination, may store, process, or share the received student data in ways that violate privacy expectations or regulations, such as sharing student work with unauthorized parties.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in student data sharing
description: Sharing student names and work content with teachers may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper consent, access controls, or data minimization principles are not followed.

title: Teacher identity exposure through grader ID
description: When a teacher records a grade, the grader ID included in the data could potentially be used to identify the teacher, especially if the grader ID is not properly anonymized or if the teacher's identity is not protected.

title: Linkability of teacher-student relationship
description: The data flow contains student ID, grader ID, and grade information. This metadata could be used to link and identify the relationship between specific teachers and students, potentially revealing sensitive information about grading patterns or student-teacher interactions.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Grade and feedback data transmitted from teacher to the web app could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly encrypted, exposing sensitive student performance information.

title: Insecure storage of student grades and feedback
description: The Grades Portal Web App receives and stores sensitive student performance data including grades and written feedback. If the system does not implement proper access controls and encryption, this data could be accessed by unauthorized personnel.

title: Lack of non-repudiation for grade submissions
description: The system may not adequately record audit trails or digital signatures for grade submissions, allowing teachers to potentially deny having submitted certain grades or feedback.

title: Student and grader identification in grade records
description: The grading service writes grade records containing student IDs and grader IDs, which explicitly identify individuals. The act of sharing this data at the source creates an identification threat.

title: Unauthorized access to grade records
description: The grade records database stores sensitive information including grades and feedback, which could be accessed by unauthorized parties. The destination element's storage and processing creates a disclosure threat.

title: Interception of grade data in transit
description: Grade records transmitted from the grading service to the database could be intercepted during transit, allowing an attacker to link students to their grades and grader information.

title: Excessive data storage in grade records
description: The database stores feedback and other information that may be more than necessary for the grading process, potentially violating data minimization principles.

title: Student identity used to identify grades data
description: Student (EE1) shares their identity to request grades, which are inherently identifying data. The act of sharing identity at the source enables identification of the student to their academic records.
assumptions: Student must authenticate to access their grades

title: Metadata in grades request could link student identity
description: Data in transit (DF8) may contain metadata (e.g., timestamps, request patterns, or partial identifiers) that could be used to link the student's identity to their grades data, even if the grades themselves are not directly exposed in transit.
assumptions: Network traffic or request metadata is observable
uncertainty_note: Depends on implementation details of the web app and network security

title: Grades data processed/stored with identifying information
description: Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives and processes grades data that is linked to the student's identity. If stored or processed without proper access controls, this could lead to unauthorized disclosure of the student's academic information.
assumptions: System stores grades with student identifiers

title: Metadata Linkability in Grade Data Transmission
description: Metadata accompanying the grade data (e.g., timestamps, session identifiers, or data structure patterns) could potentially be used to link the student's identity to their grades, even if the data itself is encrypted.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Grade data and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured (e.g., lacking TLS encryption).

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure at Source
description: The Grades Portal Web App may inadvertently disclose student grades to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, logging mechanisms, or data exposure in error messages.

title: Student Data Usurpation by Third Parties
description: Once the student receives their grades and feedback, they may share this information with unauthorized third parties (e.g., peers, employers, or family members) who could misuse the academic performance data.

title: Parent-Child Account Linkage Exploitation
description: The parent's account is linked to the child's account. When the parent requests grades, this linkage could be exploited to infer information about the child's academic performance or identity to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The linkage between parent and child accounts is not adequately protected or is visible in system logs.

title: Request Metadata Identification
description: Metadata about the request (e.g., timestamp, parent ID, child ID) in transit could be used to identify which parent is accessing which child's grades, potentially revealing sensitive information about the parent-child relationship.
assumptions: Request metadata is not properly obfuscated or encrypted during transmission.

title: Credential Interception in Transit
description: Parent credentials (e.g., authentication tokens, session data) transmitted during the login and grade request process could be intercepted by attackers, enabling unauthorized access to child's grades.
assumptions: Credentials are transmitted without adequate encryption or are vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose child's grades to unauthorized parties (e.g., other users, system administrators, or through improper logging), violating privacy expectations and potentially FERPA regulations.
assumptions: The system lacks proper access controls or has vulnerabilities in data handling.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's academic data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose sensitive academic information (grades, feedback, submission history) to the parent without proper authorization controls or verification that the parent is the legitimate guardian.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Academic data transmitted from the portal to the parent could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive student information.

title: Parent misuse of child's academic data
description: The parent receiving the data may use it for purposes beyond their intended role, such as sharing with third parties or using it for unauthorized purposes.

title: Excessive data sharing beyond necessity
description: The portal may share more detailed academic information than necessary for the parent's legitimate oversight role, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Personal data (names, emails, roles, relationships) transmitted between administrator and web app could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, enabling identification of parents and children.

title: Linkability of Parent-Child Data
description: Metadata and data in transit could be used to link parent-child relationships with other data sources, potentially revealing family connections and enabling profiling.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Destination
description: The Grades Portal Web App may store sensitive parent-child relationship data without adequate access controls, risking disclosure to unauthorized personnel or systems.

title: Data Misuse for Unauthorized Purposes
description: The process may use collected parent-child relationship data for purposes beyond the intended scope (e.g., marketing, third-party sharing) without proper consent.

title: False or Misleading Data Entry
description: Administrator may intentionally or unintentionally enter incorrect parent-child relationship data, leading to inaccurate records and potential privacy violations for affected families.

title: Metadata Linkability in Data Flow
description: The data flow from the grading service to the account directory may contain metadata (e.g., timestamps, source identifiers, or transaction IDs) that could be used to link individuals across different data flows or contexts, potentially enabling correlation attacks.

title: Identifiability from Stored Account Records
description: The account directory stores account records and parent-child relationship links that, when combined with other information, could be used to identify specific individuals and their family relationships.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Data
description: The account directory may have inadequate access controls, allowing unauthorized parties to access the stored account records and relationship links, leading to privacy violations.

title: Excessive Data Storage
description: The account directory may store more data than necessary for its purpose, including sensitive grading-related information that should be stored in a more restricted system rather than a general account directory.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are intentionally transferred to the cloud hosting provider as part of nightly backup and replication. This constitutes explicit data disclosure to a third party, raising concerns about data minimality and whether all transferred data is strictly necessary for the hosting service.

title: Linkability via Metadata in Data Transfer
description: During the nightly backup transfer, metadata about the data (e.g., timestamps, data volumes, access patterns) could be used to link or identify individuals. The account directory being transferred enables potential cross-referencing of student identities across systems.

title: Identification Risk at Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider receives account directory and grade records that contain personally identifiable information. There is a risk that the provider could identify individuals through this data, potentially for purposes beyond the intended hosting service.

title: Unnecessary Data Sharing at Source
description: The Assignment & Grading Service shares comprehensive data (full grade records, assignments, account directory) with the cloud provider. This may violate the minimality principle if not all this data is strictly required for the backup/hosting purpose, creating avoidable disclosure risk.

title: Linkability of grade records across views
description: Grade records in transit may contain metadata or identifiers that allow linking student, parent, and teacher views, potentially revealing relationships between parties.

title: Identifiability of individuals in grade data
description: Grade records may contain personally identifiable information (student IDs, names) that could be used to identify individuals during data transfer.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade records
description: Assignment & Grading Service may disclose grade records to unauthorized parties or in unauthorized contexts when building student, parent, and teacher views.

title: Excessive data collection in view generation
description: The grading service may collect and process more grade record data than necessary for building the intended views, violating data minimization principles.

title: Unauthorized use of grade records
description: The grading service may use grade records for purposes beyond the intended view generation, such as profiling or sharing with third parties.
